title.en: The Little Bookshop by the Station

sentences.en: In front of the station there is a small bookshop.
Every morning an old man opens the shop at seven.
A white cat always sleeps on top of the old books.
One day a child came into the shop.
"Is that cat for sale too?" the child asked.
The old man laughed and said, "No, that one is the manager."
The child's eyes went wide, and they asked the cat, "Manager, how much is this book?"
Without saying anything, the cat climbed down from the books.
The old man said, "The manager says it's fine, so a hundred yen will do."
The child bought the book and started coming to the shop every Saturday.
These days, the cat sleeps on the child's lap.

title.en: A Promise on a Rainy Day

sentences.en: I don't like rain.
But the rain of that one day is still a precious memory.
In the spring of my first year of high school, I was waiting for a train at the station.
Suddenly it started raining hard, and without an umbrella I was stuck.
Just then, a boy I didn't know let me under his blue umbrella.
"We're on the same train, right?" he said.
On the train we talked about music.
He said, "Next Sunday, if it rains, let's meet here again."
The next Sunday, the sky was clear.
I felt a little sad.
But when I went to the station, there he was, holding the blue umbrella.
"It didn't rain, but a promise is a promise."
Ten years on, we are together, rain or shine.

title.en: A Night at the Hot-Spring Inn

sentences.en: Last autumn, my father and I went to a hot spring in the mountains.
The inn was old, and we were the only guests.
After dinner, my father fell asleep right away.
I woke at two in the morning to a sound.
Someone was walking down the corridor.
The footsteps were slowly coming closer to my room.
I was so scared I couldn't make a sound.
The door slid open a little.
Something white came in and licked my face.
When I turned on the light, it was the inn's big dog.
The next morning the landlady said, "Our dog just loves guests. Sorry about that."
"I didn't hear a thing," said my father, and ate his hot-spring egg.

title.en: First Day at the New Company

sentences.en: Today is my first day at a new company.
I got up at six and put on new clothes.
I ran to the station and got on the train.
When I arrived, the department head said, "You're the new one. First, coffee."
I hurried to make coffee for ten people.
But he laughed: "No, no. It was for you. First, take a break."
In the morning I learnt how to use the computer.
At lunch I had the fish set meal at a nearby place with the people from my department.
In the afternoon I listened to an important talk.
I didn't really understand, but I nodded whenever everyone else did.
At five, the boss said, "Good work today. Tomorrow, again, just make coffee for yourself."
I think I'm going to like this company.

title.jp: おじいさんの古い時計

sentences.en: My grandfather lived in the oldest house in town.
Inside the house there was a big clock.
Grandfather and Grandmother bought it when they were young.
Every day the clock ran five minutes slow.

tokens.m: the better choice (it would be better to)

sentences.en: "You should get it fixed," I said, but Grandfather shook his head.
"This clock is like your grandmother, a bit slow. That's fine as it is."
Grandmother died before I was born.
Last winter, Grandfather was gone too.
The clock is now in my room.
It still runs five minutes slow every day, so sometimes I miss my train.
But I have no intention of fixing it.
Because when I hear the clock, I feel I can hear Grandfather's voice.
"That's fine as it is."
At the end of March, it snowed.
White snow settled on the trees that had only just blossomed.
"It's spring, so why?" my little sister said, looking outside.
"Winter came to say goodbye," Mum answered.
My sister thought for a moment, then went outside.
And she made a tiny snowman and put a single blossom on it.
"Winter, take some spring home with you."
The next day the snow had melted, and only the blossom was left on the ground.
